title: Tight Security Bounds for Two-Round LDT
summary: Two-round LDT achieves beyond-birthday security for restricted query sizes, but the proven bound is non-tight and its exact security across those sizes remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine tight security bounds for the two-round LDT construction ($2\text{-LDT}$) over query sizes in $[n,3n/2)$. Existing results establish beyond-birthday security, with $2n/3$-bit security for evaluations of size around $n$ and $n/2$-bit security for evaluations of size around $3n/2$, but explicitly state that the bound is not tight. A birthday-bound attack is known at the parameter value $s=n-1$, indicating that security decreases as $s$ increases. The unresolved task is to derive matching attacks or sharper proofs that characterize the exact security across these input-length regimes.

scope.domain: Security analysis of the two-round LDT variable-length domain extender in symmetric cryptography.
parameters: n: baseline size defining the query-size range and the reported bit-security levels
s: parameter whose increase is associated with lower security; a birthday-bound attack is known at s = n − 1
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive matching attacks or sharper proofs that determine the exact security throughout the stated input-length regimes.

citations.label: Short Variable Length Domain Extenders with Beyond Birthday Bound Security

progress.summary: The source proves beyond-birthday security for two-round LDT, reporting two-thirds-n-bit security for evaluations around n and one-half-n-bit security around three-halves n. It calls the bound non-tight and notes a birthday-bound attack at s = n − 1.
